_meta.note: Two emergent capabilities made real. (PO) Parity as a differential-testing oracle: a seeded, deterministic generator produces varied dag.json+events.jsonl and asserts node == python on every shared pure surface across many seeds — two implementations of one spec are each other's oracle, so any disagreement is a real bug. The gate has teeth because a mutation self-test injects a known node<->python divergence (via the existing HB_PY_SRC seam) and asserts the fuzzer CATCHES it. (RR) Verifiable-reward + model-regression: pure functions over the event log turn each gate evaluation into a deterministically-labeled reward record, and turn two bench scorecards into a regression verdict. Reward trusts the log's gate verdict, never the backend's self-report. Python-only analysis tooling, like bench itself (documented divergence, not a parity gap).

tasks.title: Seeded deterministic case generator
tasks.description: Spec-first: write tests/gen-parity-case.py — given an integer seed and a target dir, it emits a structurally-varied but WELL-FORMED .hb/dag.json + .hb/events.jsonl; given a seed and '-' it prints the same bundle to stdout (for a temp-dir-free determinism check). It uses ONLY the seed (a small local PRNG; no Math.random, no time, no wall-clock ts) so the same seed always yields byte-identical output. Varies: phase count, tasks/phase (<=8), sparse requires edges, gate shapes (behavioral / review-blocked), and a plausible event sequence (initialized, task_started/done/failed, gate_passed/gate_failed, review_passed). This generator IS the spec of the input space the oracle explores; the input space (well-formed DAGs) is documented, not silently capped.

tasks.title: Fuzz harness over both runtimes
tasks.description: Write tests/parity-fuzz.sh: for N seeds (N = arg, small default), generate a case with tests/gen-parity-case.py, copy the node templates into the temp .hb (as tests/parity.sh does), run the case through BOTH runtimes on every shared pure surface (audit, lint, state, next, ready, report, diagnose), normalize identically to tests/parity.sh, and assert node == python. Print one line per seed and print 'FUZZ-PARITY-OK:<N>' only when every seed agreed on every surface; exit non-zero on the first divergence, printing the seed and the diverging surface so it reproduces.

tasks.title: Mutation self-test (the oracle has teeth)
tasks.description: Add a --selftest mode to tests/parity-fuzz.sh that runs TWO passes in one invocation and requires BOTH to bind the teeth: (1) the fuzzer on the UN-mutated py/src must agree across the seeds and print 'SELFTEST-CLEAN-OK'; (2) then copy py/src to a temp dir, inject a deliberate divergence into one pure function, point HB_PY_SRC at that mutant, run the SAME seeds, and print 'SELFTEST-CAUGHT:<surface>' only when the fuzzer actually detects the injected node<->python divergence. Requiring a legitimate clean pass AND a caught divergence in the same run means an unconditional echo cannot satisfy it — proving a green fuzzer can go red.

Update docs/howto/keep-the-runtimes-in-parity.md (the generative-oracle method, linking the harness), docs/dev-tests.md (the T75 row + a note in the Parity section), and planning/parity-notes.md. Keep tests/parity.sh green (unchanged).

tasks.title: Author the reward+regression proof (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/reward-regression.sh — a self-verifying proof that builds a KNOWN synthetic event log (a gate_passed and a gate_failed) and asserts 'hb reward' yields exactly the matching labeled records (one passed=true, one passed=false — the deterministic log verdict, not a self-report); and builds two KNOWN scorecards (a clearly-worse candidate vs a baseline, and an equal one) and asserts the regression comparator flags regressed=true for the worse and regressed=false for the equal. Prints 'REWARD-REGRESSION-OK' only when every assertion holds. Written before the implementation.

tasks.title: Reward extractor (pure) + CLI
tasks.description:
Implement a PURE core reward_records(events, dag) in py/src/heartbeat/bench.py (mirroring how score uses st.project): one reward record per gate_passed/gate_failed event — {gate, phase, passed, actor, ts}. passed is the deterministic log verdict (gate_passed=true / gate_failed=false), NEVER the backend's self-report. phase is NOT on the event, so derive it from the dag via st.phase_by_gate_exit(dag, gate). actor/ts come from the event when present, else null (the gate.sh path adds no actor — record that honestly, do not fabricate). Add rewards(hbdir) that reads the log+dag and calls the pure core, and wire 'hb reward --dir

[--json]' in py/src/heartbeat/cli.py to emit the records (JSONL by default, JSON array with --json).

tasks.title: Regression comparator (pure) + CLI
tasks.description: Implement regressions(cards, baseline_label) in py/src/heartbeat/bench.py: a PURE comparator over bench scorecards returning {baseline, candidate, regressed, deltas} per non-baseline card — regressed=true when a candidate clears fewer gates OR completes fewer phases OR has more task_failures than the baseline. Wire 'hb bench --baseline <label>' in py/src/heartbeat/cli.py so the output includes the regression verdict against that card.

GATE_PO.desc: The generative oracle agrees across seeds, is deterministic, and provably catches an injected node<->python divergence.

review.prompt: Refute that PO is done: does the fuzzer actually COMPARE both runtimes, or can it print FUZZ-PARITY-OK without ever diverging? does the generator produce VARIED inputs per seed, or the same trivial DAG every time? is the generator truly deterministic (same seed -> identical bytes), or does a ts/random leak in? does --selftest really inject a divergence and require the fuzzer to catch it, or is SELFTEST-CAUGHT printed unconditionally?

criteria.desc: node == python across generated seeds (agreement marker)
the oracle passes clean AND catches an injected divergence in one run (teeth bound)
the generator is deterministic (same seed -> identical output)

GATE_RR.desc: Reward records carry the deterministic log verdict (not self-report), and the regression comparator flags a worse candidate while clearing an equal one.

review.prompt: Refute that RR is done: is 'reward' a trivial gate_passed count, or a per-evaluation labeled record tied to the log's verdict? could reward ever reflect the backend's self-report instead of the gate_passed/gate_failed event? does the regression comparator detect a genuinely-worse candidate AND clear an equal one, or does it vacuously return one answer? are rewards/regressions PURE over the log (no re-running the backend)?

criteria.desc: the reward+regression proof passes (known log -> exact labels; worse -> regressed, equal -> not)
hb reward is a real subcommand
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m heartbeat.cli reward --help 2>&1 | grep -qi 'usage'

criteria.desc: reward_records is pure over (events,dag): correct passed labels AND phase DERIVED from the dag (not the event)
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from heartbeat import bench; dag={'phases':[{'id':'P0','gate_exit':'G0','tasks':[]}],'gates':{'G0':{}}}; evs=[{'event':'gate_passed','gate':'G0'},{'event':'gate_failed','gate':'G0'}]; r=bench.reward_records(evs,dag); assert [x['passed'] for x in r]==[True,False], r; assert all(x['phase']=='P0' for x in r), r"

criteria.desc: the regression comparator flags a worse candidate as regressed
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from heartbeat import bench; base={'label':'base','gate_passed':2,'phases_done':2,'task_failures':0}; worse={'label':'cand','gate_passed':0,'phases_done':0,'task_failures':3}; r=bench.regressions([base,worse],'base'); assert any(x['candidate']=='cand' and x['regressed'] for x in r), r"

criteria.desc: the regression comparator CLEARS an equal candidate (regressed=false — both directions)
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from heartbeat import bench; base={'label':'base','gate_passed':2,'phases_done':2,'task_failures':0}; same={'label':'cand','gate_passed':2,'phases_done':2,'task_failures':0}; r=bench.regressions([base,same],'base'); assert all(not x['regressed'] for x in r if x['candidate']=='cand'), r"
